entities.summary: Richard Croke was an English classical scholar and royal tutor who played a crucial role in shaping the educational landscape of Elizabethan England. Born in 1520, Croke received his education at Cambridge University, where he became a prominent figure in the translation and publication of classical texts. His work, particularly his translation of the 'Iliad' and 'Odyssey', had a significant impact on the literary and cultural development of the time. Croke's legacy can be seen in the many scholars and writers who followed in his footsteps, including William Shakespeare and John Donne. His contributions to the field of classical studies have endured for centuries, with many of his works still studied and admired today. As a testament to his enduring influence, Croke's name is still invoked by scholars and educators today, who recognize his importance in shaping the educational priorities of the Elizabethan era. The legacy of Richard Croke serves as a reminder of the power of education and the importance of preserving classical knowledge for future generations.
